fields.name: Gadādhara dāsa (Puruṣottama-māhātmya)
fields.place: Gaṇisiṁha near Indrāṇī (by Agradvīpa); Purī; Mākhanpur (Purī district)
fields.notes: Of Gaṇisiṁha near Indrāṇī (Agradvīpa); son of Kamalākānta dāsa, with whom he lived at Purī; brother of Kāśīrāma dāsa (the Bengali Mahābhārata) and of Kṛṣṇadāsa. Wrote about 1778 the Puruṣottama-māhātmya, opening with the praise of Gaurāṅga and gathering Purāṇic evidence of His divinity. (The Gadādhara dāsa of Vṛndāvana, Vaiṣṇava-vandanā 70, has his own record since 11-11-2026.)

fields.place: Born at Sonāmukhī (Bankura); Calcutta (Metropolitan College); Kashmir (from 1893)
fields.notes: Born 1865 at Sonāmukhī to Jayarāma Bandyopādhyāya and Bhagavatī Sundarī; lost his father at two; studied in Calcutta; from 1893 served the King of Kashmir, where Lālā Aṭalabihārī Nandī, struck by his supernatural powers, became his disciple. Life told in the book Pāgala Haranātha and by Bhāgavatacandra Mitra, Akiñcana Nandī and Kṣīrodacandra Bhaṭṭācārya.

fields.aka: Puruṣottama, Madanalatā gopī, Madanālasā sakhī, Mahābala
fields.works: Kāñcī-kāverī (historical kāvya on King Puruṣottamadeva's conquest of Kāñcī)
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa poet of Orissa, author of the Kāñcī-kāverī (Caitanya-bandanā of S. Rath). Oṛiyā texts make him Madanalatā gopī (Guru-bhakti-gītā) or Madanālasā sakhī and Mahābala (Svarūpa-varṇana; an Oṛiyā Caitanya-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā). Called a paṇḍita and a brāhmaṇa in Dāśarathi dāsa's Braja-bihāra.
